needs.thing: a boatman's house near the city landing, with a room inside and a locked back room
needs.quests: the fourth main quest, "The Sour Spring", and every later main quest
needs.does: The player is given work by a small household of spies who pass themselves off as boatmen, and brings back what they ask for.
needs.why: Not met. The house nearest the city landing, about 50 metres from where the raft-master stands, can be entered, but its door shows "House" like every house in the town, inside is one room with no back room, and nothing marks it as a boatman's.
needs.fit: That house (the tally-keeper Ixtul-Bei's household lives there today) could be the spies' house: the story can meet them in its one room. The boatmen's lodge, a moored ship about 76 metres from the landing whose door shows "Ship", is the other building a player would tie to boatmen.
needs.narrow: Partly. A name on the house (the name its door shows) and the household's people placed inside are narrow changes. A locked back room is not: the house has one room, so the story should keep its secret behind a locked chest or a locked door the room already has.
needs.story_thing: a boatman's house near the city landing, with a room inside and a locked back room

sight.said: none: the boats' spot has no house door, and the one house seen is far from the landing

needs.thing: a spring at the foot of the town's sacred tree, shut behind a low wicker door that locks, with a dipper on its edge and a guard beside it
needs.quests: the fourth main quest, "The Sour Spring", and the endings of the main story
needs.does: The player gets a drink of water from a spring the town has shut away: by picking its lock, by talking past its guard, or by buying a gourd of it from the sap-seller.

signs.detail: the water-carrier Ruxa-Neel and the sap-seller Wujeel speak of it

needs.why: Not met. The town's sacred tree stands at its middle (a small tree of the sacred kind, where a shrine's blessing is given), but nothing at its foot is a spring: no pool or water, no small door that locks, no dipper and no guard post beside it. The nearest guard stand is about 98 metres away.
needs.fit: The sacred tree itself, where most of the townsfolk stand by day, among them the water-carrier who says the spring is not used. The story could put the shut water at the tree's foot as a sealed basin or a locked water jar, guarded by one of the levy.
needs.narrow: Yes, as placed things: a basin or small pool piece and a wicker gate that locks at the tree's foot, and one guard's day spot moved beside it. No redraft. If no piece we hold reads as a spring, the story should name what is placed instead (a sealed basin).
needs.story_thing: the city tree's spring shut behind a low wicker door that locks, with a dipper on its lip and a guard's post beside it

sight.said: none: a sacred tree, but no spring, wicker door, dipper or guard

needs.thing: one crocodile on the mud below the city landing
needs.quests: the fourth main quest, "The Sour Spring"
needs.does: The player kills one crocodile on the mud below the city landing to take its gall to the sap-seller.
needs.why: Not met. The place files hold no creatures; the river edge and the mud below the landing are there.
needs.fit: The river edge at the city landing, where the raft-master Poles-Upriver stands; or the wild ground outside the town, where the world's own beasts already are.
needs.narrow: Yes, if a place can hold one placed creature (today the place files hold people only); otherwise the story sends the player outside the town for the gall.

needs.thing: a place by that spring where a few elders can stand
needs.quests: the endings of the main story
needs.does: At the end of the main story the town's elders gather by the spring, and the player sees who came.
needs.why: Not met while there is no spring. The open ground round the sacred tree is where about 30 townsfolk stand by day, the town's two assembly elders (Hixee-Ra and Ooxa-Leet) among them, but a player cannot tell the elders from anyone else there.
needs.fit: The open ground round the sacred tree, where the two elders already stand by day.
needs.narrow: Yes: it follows once the spring is at the tree's foot; the elders are already placed there.
needs.story_thing: a place by the spring where a few elders can stand

sight.said: none: no spring is seen; the tree is only a guess

needs.thing: a hall of the tree-healers that can be entered, with a spot inside where their leader stands
needs.does: The player joins a faction of healers who travel to sick sacred trees: its leader gives each job and takes each report inside its hall.

signs.detail: the healer Taleeka-Ma heals and sells spell tomes there, and she and the sap-seller Wujeel both name it and its leader

needs.why: Not met. The healer Taleeka-Ma, who heals and sells spell tomes, works inside a cave at the north-west edge of the town beside an arcane enchanter, and two guards stand at its mouth. But its door is a moss-covered cave door, and looking at it the game shows "Quick Test Cell" (a leftover test name); nothing names it a hall.
needs.story_know: its door is named "Tree-Minders' Hall"; Taleeka-Ma heals and sells tomes at it; Taleeka-Ma and Wujeel both name it and Okeeh-Ja
needs.fit: The cave itself: it can be entered, the healer already works there by the enchanter the town promises for its hall, and the faction's leader could stand inside. The story can call it the tree-minders' cave, or keep 'hall' once the name is changed. It is about 520 metres from the sacred tree.
needs.narrow: Yes: renaming the room (the name its door shows) to "Tree-Minders' Hall" is a narrow change, and it also takes away the test name a player would see today; the leader is one person placed inside.
needs.story_thing: the tree-minders' hall as a building that can be entered, with a place inside where Okeeh-Ja stands

sight.said: a temple or guild hall at best; its door's name 'Quick Test Cell' looks like an unfinished placeholder, and nothing says tree or healing

needs.quests: every quest of the line; the second spot from the third quest

the healers' leader calls her the root-tender at the door; the elder Hixee-Ra speaks first and says who she is

needs.why: Not met. Xilsa-Jee, the young root-tender, stands by day in the crowd round the sacred tree, about 500 metres from the cave door, and nothing shows her at work on roots. The elder Hixee-Ra stands in the same crowd.
needs.story_know: Xilsa-Jee is seen clearing creepers from roots (D people); Okeeh-Ja names her as "the root-tender at the door"; Hixee-Ra speaks first when MR03 is reported and says who she is
needs.fit: Both are placed and can be spoken to at the sacred tree. The story can meet them there, at the tree whose roots she tends, rather than at the hall's door.
needs.narrow: Yes: moving the two women's day spots to beside the cave door is a person's routine change, not a redraft.
needs.story_thing: a spot among the roots by the hall's door where Xilsa-Jee stands, and from MR03 a spot beside it for Hixee-Ra
